newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Great River to expand apparel plant.
newsitem.headline: Great River to expand apparel plant.

text.p: Indonesian garment firm PT Great River International (GRI) said on Monday it would invest 45 billion rupiah to expand its apparel plant capacity.
It said in a statement it had applied to the Investment Coordinating Board for permission to increase plant capacity to 50 million pieces of apparel by 1998 from the current 24 million pieces.
"The plant expansion will be at three sites ... in Cibinong, Cikarang and Purwakarta. The number of employees will reach 15,000 from the current 12,000," the firm said.
It also said it was optimistic about achieving its net income target of 26 billion rupiah and its sales target of 250 billion rupiah by the end of 1996.
"Having a net profit of 12.9 billion rupiah in the first half of 1996, GRI is optimistic it will achieve net income and sales targets for 1996," the company statement said.
GRI is a garment manufacturer and currently holds about 50 international brand licences.

In early August, it signed a joint venture agreement with PT Indomulti, part of the Salim Group, for two projects valued at 200 billion rupiah to operate a department store and establish a distribution company for sports shoes and sportsware.

The joint venture will operate a 26,000 sq metre department store in the Senayan Square complex under the management of Japan's Hanshin department store. It is due to start operating by the end of 1997 or early 1998.
Great River president director Sunyoto Tanudjaja said the firm would also continue to expand its own distribution and retailing systems through direct selling and franchising.
"Direct selling will include 30,000 apparel dealers by 1998 from the current 10,000 dealers. We will have 100 franchised outlets before the end of 1998," he added.
